findings.suggested_fix: Base T-12's Known entry on design CO-7 ('Read only; no migration'), or move it to Assumed. Do not cite C5/C10 for read-only.
findings.text: T-12's Known line cites C5 and C10 as the basis for 'the design only reads the appointment table'. C5 says appointment_event records changes, and C10 says the index exists. Neither states that the change is read-only.

cites.quote: Reads of visit history are not attributed to a user.
appointment_event already records every change with actor (C5), and no new write is added.

findings.suggested_fix: State T-6 as accepted: no read audit exists in the MVP, and none is added. Drop C5 as a supporting control.
findings.text: The T-6 threat is about reads not being attributed. Its rationale points to appointment_event, which records only changes, so it does not address reads. In effect the mitigation is risk acceptance and should say so plainly.

findings.text: Claim C7 (logs never carry request bodies) is declared, but no threat or mitigation uses it. Either the log-disclosure angle for the new field is missing, or the claim is unused.

rubric_items.reason: All seven design components (CO-1 to CO-7) are named and each has at least one threat. The PII-bearing repo, service, route and list type each have an information-disclosure threat.
The threats fit their components: a wider SELECT, reuse of the detail type, subquery SQL input, MVP spoofing. T-9 now names an actor. T-10 is still a display-correctness defect with a STRIDE label.

Mitigations are cited existing controls or labelled new controls for implement. T-5 now honestly says none and accepts the risk. T-6 and T-12 lean on appointment_event, which only covers writes and so does not address those threats.
The MVP sign-in gap is U-1 and is asked as Q-01 with options and a default. The out-of-inputs context files are disclosed in Unknown.
Threats are now ordered by risk, highest first. The body matches the frontmatter, and the Known/Assumed split is clear.
